scope: 2021 first-printing multiplayer full core: all four Oaths and true Visions, Conspiracy, citizenship, Campaign, first/later setup and Chronicle; official supplied base errata applied; no bots or expansions.

findings.source_rule: Step 5.5.8 applies victory battle-plan effects to the victorious player, including a victorious defender. It then discards applicable end-discard plans used by either player, including the defeated attacker.
findings.existing_mapping: coverage_map[Law 5.5.8 end effects] maps only to Q016. Q016 explicitly asks what happens after an attacker wins and ends with the terse instruction Victory effects then end-discard plans. Q038 covers an attacker defeat and the lack of ordinary defender target-taking, but omits defender victory battle-plan effects and end-discard from both sides.
findings.why_novel: This is the other source-defined outcome branch of the final Campaign step: a defender victory does not skip 5.5.8. It is not another roll, force count, named-card substitution, or combination of unrelated mechanics. A reader who incorrectly treats all Campaign victory consequences as attacker-only can answer Q016 and Q038 exactly as keyed.
findings.consequence: The benchmark currently permits omission of a victorious defender's battle-plan effects and mistaken retention of an end-discard plan merely because its user lost.
findings.recommended_action: Add A01 (suggested new ID Q093) and map Law 5.5.8 to it as well as Q016. Reopen zero-addition passes after adjudicating this addition.

proposed_additions.question: The attacker loses a Campaign. The defender used a battle plan saying “If you're victorious,” and both players used plans saying “At end, discard [card name].” What resolves after the roll, in what order, and does losing let the attacker keep their end-discard plan?
proposed_additions.expected_answer: Resolve the defeated attacker's losses first: kill half of the warbands remaining in their force, rounded down, keep the survivors on their board, then resolve any battle plans they used that say “If you're defeated.” Skip the attacker's target-taking step because the attacker lost. In Step 8, resolve the victorious defender's “If you're victorious” battle plans. Then discard the applicable “At end, discard [card name]” plans used by either player. The defeated attacker still discards such a plan; the end-discard instruction does not require its user to have won. Apply the text of each effect, including any optional parts.
material_facts: Attacker defeat resolves losses and any defeated battle-plan effects before the final battle-plan step.
The attacker's target-taking step is skipped after an attacker defeat.
The victorious defender resolves their used If you're victorious battle plans in Step 8.
Applicable At end, discard plans from either side discard after victory effects, including a plan used by the defeated attacker.

key_review.scope_limit: No unsupported contemporary web rulings, absent card database entries or expansion rules imported.

coverage_assessment.novelty_assessment: The ten marked historical duplicates are correctly excluded from novelty. The remaining bank spans all requested core domains; no further source-backed independent additions were found beyond A01. Do not count mere new numbers, cards or mechanical conjunctions as new coverage.
coverage_assessment.mapping_assessment: The ledger has a mapping entry for every core procedural section, but a section-level mapping is insufficient for Law 5.5.8 because Q016 exercises only the attacker-victory branch. Other mapped source procedures and consequential exceptions were accounted for by the bank, often across multiple questions.
coverage_assessment.stopping_passes_6_7: Not independently validated as saturation: their zero counts miss the defender-victory branch of Law 5.5.8. Their recorded counts can remain historical, but they do not justify a current saturation PASS until A01 is adjudicated and fresh zero-addition sweeps are completed.
